rules.callsign: US/CA/Caribbean only, when the lookup finds nothing: a station callsign in brackets ('NBC 5 (KFYR) Minot') matches feeds named after that callsign ('KFYR', 'KFYR-TV'); when several channels share it, the one whose name or network appears in the provider name wins
rules.closed: a closed channel never supplies its own guide. Fallback (5): when every closed channel a name matches names a live successor (replaced_by, followed up to 3 times) and that is one channel, the name resolves to the successor with method 'replaced_by' (the stream now carries it: 'FOX' in a Turkish list -> NOW). Otherwise explain_closed only explains the name
rules.confidence: one channel id = high; several ids = ambiguous (owner review, never applied automatically)
rules.country_tag: a leading '(MX)'-style bracket with a Latin American country code in US, CA, LATAM or CARIB lists puts that country first, then market_countries['LATAM'] (LATAM rules); and in group_markets: a leading section tag naming a country ('|NIGERIA| ', 'IQ: ', 'DSTV | ') replaces market_countries[market] with that one country for every step; the tag is country_tags[TAG] or a two-letter code listed in market_countries[market]. Without a tag, each lookup method pools all market_countries (not first country wins), so a name found in two countries is ambiguous
rules.explain_closed: a name matching only a closed channel is reported as closed (with replaced_by), never as a guide match
rules.fallbacks: only when the lookup finds nothing, in order: (1) aliases[market] then aliases['*']: replace the first matching pattern and repeat the lookup; (2) singular/plural of the last word (>= 4 letters); (3) language_variants[market]: '<name> <variant>' in any country, only when the name ends in a market code (dropped first, e.g. 'CGTN FR'), or the plain name has at least 6 letters/digits and is not itself a channel; a result counts only when it is one channel; (4) a trailing code of the channel's own market (bare_market_codes[market]) is dropped, with a quality word before it ('ZDF HD DE' -> 'zdf'), and the lookup repeated; (2b, after (2)) the sport word in its other spellings sport/sports/spor; (3b, after (3)) a name ending in a number plus language_variants[market] looked up in the market's own countries only ('beIN Sports 1' -> 'beIN Sports 1 Turk' in TR; also preferred whenever a numbered name is otherwise found only by broadcast_area, i.e. as a foreign channel broadcasting into the market); (6, last) '<name> 1' as '<name>' when '<name> 2' exists in the market. Any step: when candidates differ only by a 4K/UHD version and the provider name has no 4K/UHD marker, the plain channel is chosen (method suffix ':plain_not_4k')
rules.lookup: market_key(name, market) == normalised name, alt name, or base name + feed name of a channel in one of market_countries[market] (exact or ignoring spaces/punctuation); then decoration-only equality; then channels whose feed broadcasts into those countries
rules.precedence: below user manual mappings, provider tvg-id exact and published crosswalks
rules.transliteration: Cyrillic and Greek names and alternative names are also indexed in Latin script (transliterate()), so 'Rossiya 1' and 'EPT 1' match

scope: UK and Europe channels, plus feeds of other channels that broadcast there
